tool.name: AlphaFind Protein Search
tool.description: Search AlphaFind API for structurally similar proteins
tool.command: python3 '$__tool_directory__/alphafind_search.py' --query '$query' --index '$index' --mode '$mode' #if $filtering.organism --filter-organism '$filtering.organism' #end if #if $filtering.tax_id --filter-tax-id $filtering.tax_id #end if #if $filtering.gene_name --filter-gene-name '$filtering.gene_name' #end if #if $filtering.cath_annotation --filter-cath-annotation '$filtering.cath_annotation' #end if #if $searching.k --option-k $searching.k #end if --timeout ${searching.timeout} --sort-by ${sorting.sort_by} --sort-order ${sorting.sort_order} --quiet --output '$output'

param.name: query
param.label: Protein Query
param.help: Enter a UniProt protein ID (e.g., P0A6F5, Q8Y547, Q9SBL1)

param.name: index
param.label: Search Index
param.help: Select one index type to search. Defaults to 'Full-chain AlphaFold structures'. With 'domains', a UniProt accession (e.g. Q73WU1) is resolved to all its TED domains, each domain searched independently, and results merged into one CSV with an extra 'domain' column naming the source TED ID.

param.name: mode
param.label: Result Type
param.help: 'Approximate results' returns kNN hits immediately, without TM-scores or experimental-structure mapping. 'TM-scores and experimental structures' waits until TM-scores are computed for every result and adds the experimental-structure (PDB) mapping; this can take a long time for large k.

param.name: organism
param.label: Organism Name
param.help: Filter by organism scientific name: the 'Scientific name' of a species-rank taxon per UniProt taxonomy (https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/?query=rank:species), e.g., 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'

param.name: gene_name
param.label: Gene Name
param.help: Filter by gene name exactly as AlphaFind stores it: the whole name, with the same capitalisation. Copy it from the gene_name column of earlier AlphaFind results, e.g. 'gpgS', 'MAP_2569c'. A name taken from UniProt may not match, because UniProt can list a different name than the one AlphaFind indexed.

param.name: cath_annotation
param.label: CATH Annotation
param.help: Filter by CATH annotation (only applied when using 'domains' index)

param.name: k
param.label: Number of Similar Proteins
param.help: Maximum number of similar proteins to return (k). Note: API can return up to 5000 results.

param.name: timeout
param.label: Timeout (seconds)
param.help: Maximum total time to wait for the API. With 'TM-scores and experimental structures' this covers the search and all lazy TM-score computations.

param.name: sort_by
param.label: Sort Results By
param.help: Choose how to order the results. TM-Score sorting needs TM-scores: with 'Approximate results' the results are sorted by KNN similarity instead.

tool.help:
**AlphaFind Protein Search**
This tool searches the AlphaFind API for structurally similar proteins based on 3D structural similarity.
-----
**What is AlphaFind?**
AlphaFind is a service for searching protein structures using AlphaFold predictions. It uses structural embeddings to find proteins with similar 3D conformations.
-----
**Input Parameters**
* **Protein Query**: A UniProt protein ID (e.g., P0A6F5, Q8Y547, Q9SBL1)
* **Search Index**: Choose which structural databases to search: - *Chains*: Full protein chains (recommended) - *Chains 90%*: Chains filtered to 90% sequence identity - *Chains 80%*: Chains filtered to 80% sequence identity - *Chains 70%*: Chains filtered to 70% sequence identity - *Domains*: Protein domains (independent structural units)
* **Result Type**: - *Approximate results*: fast. Returns the kNN hits right away, without TM-scores, alignment metrics or experimental-structure mapping. - *TM-scores and experimental structures* (default): slow. Waits until TM-scores are computed for every result and adds the experimental-structure (PDB) mapping. Large k can take tens of minutes.
* **Optional Filters**: Narrow your search results - *Organism Name*: Filter by organism scientific name — the "Scientific name" of a species-rank taxon per UniProt taxonomy (https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/?query=rank:species), e.g., 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis' - *Taxonomy ID*: Filter by NCBI taxonomy ID (numeric) - *Gene Name*: Filter by gene name exactly as AlphaFind stores it — the whole name, with the same capitalisation (e.g. 'gpgS', 'MAP_2569c'). The reliable source is the *gene_name* column of earlier AlphaFind results. A name taken from UniProt may not match, because UniProt can list a different name than the one AlphaFind indexed: for example UniProt lists K5B7Z4 as 'C731_3243', but AlphaFind stores it as 'gpgS'. - *CATH Annotation*: Filter by CATH structural classification (domains only)
* **Search Options**: - *Number of Similar Proteins*: Control result size (1-5000). Note that even with low k, the API may return all available matches up to 5000. - *Timeout*: Maximum wait time (60-7200 seconds, default 3600). Mainly matters for *TM-scores and experimental structures*: large lazy TM-score batches can take a long time.
* **Domains index note**: With `domains`, the tool resolves a UniProt accession to all its TED domains and runs one search per domain (in both result types). If the protein has no TED domains, the result is empty — this is expected behavior, not an error.
* **Sorting**: - *KNN Similarity*: Sort by embedding similarity score - *TM-Score*: Sort by structural alignment TM-score. Only available with *TM-scores and experimental structures*; with *Approximate results* there are no TM-scores, so results are sorted by KNN similarity instead.
-----
**Output Format**
*Approximate results* produce a CSV with 9 columns: query, index_type, target_id, score, organism, tax_id, gene_name, protein_name, avg_plddt. With the `domains` index three more follow: chopping, cath_annotation, and domain (the source TED ID).
*TM-scores and experimental structures* produce a CSV with 21 columns (22 with `domains`, adding `domain`; the internal API `tar_index` field is omitted):
- query_id: Unique query identifier - index_type: Index type used - page_number: Page number (internal) - target_id: Target protein ID - score: KNN similarity score (0-1) - organism: Target protein organism - tax_id: Taxonomy ID - gene_name: Gene symbol - protein_name: Protein name - avg_plddt: AlphaFold prediction quality - tm_score_query: TM-score (query as reference) - tm_score_target: TM-score (target as reference) - rmsd: Root-mean-square deviation - sequential_identity: Sequence alignment identity - aligned_residues: Aligned residue ratio - status: Computation status - created_at: Computation start time - completed_at: Computation end time - has_experimental_structure: Experimental structure available - pdb_ids: PDB identifiers - chopping: Domain boundaries (if domains)
**Lazy TM-score computation**
TM-scores are computed lazily by the API — initially only for the first few targets. With *TM-scores and experimental structures* the tool automatically pages through all results and waits until every page reports its computations complete, so the CSV always contains full TM-score coverage. For large result sets this can add substantial wall-clock time; consider raising the timeout for such queries.
-----
**Important Notes**
* This is a web-based API. The tool requires internet connectivity to https://alphafind.ics.muni.cz * Computations may take from seconds to several minutes depending on query complexity * Results are cached by the API, so repeated queries may complete faster * The API can return up to 5000 results even with a low k value * TM-score > 0.5 indicates significant structural similarity * TM-score > 0.8 indicates very high structural similarity
-----
**Examples**
1. **Basic search**: Query protein P0A6F5 with default settings
2. **Find similar proteins in specific organism**:
- Query: Q8Y547 - Organism: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
3. **Domain-level search**:
- Query: F8U1Q0 - Index: domains - CATH annotation: 1.10.8.10
4. **High-confidence results**:
- Query: P9WGR1 - Sort by: TM-Score - Sort order: Descending
-----
**References**
* AlphaFind API: https://alphafind.ics.muni.cz * AlphaFold DB: https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk * TM-Score paper: Yang & Skolnick, 2004
-----
**Troubleshooting**
* **"Protein not found"**: The query ID may not exist in AlphaFold DB or lacks embedding vectors. Verify the UniProt ID. * **Timeout exceeded**: Increase the timeout value in Search Options. * **Empty results**: When nothing matches, the job still succeeds and the dataset holds only the CSV header row. Your filters may be too restrictive, or no similar proteins exist with the specified criteria. For *Gene Name*, check that the name is copied exactly from the *gene_name* column of earlier AlphaFind results (see above). * **"Search failed"**: The API encountered an error. Try again or check the API status.
